case_content.title: Case Metadata
case_content.content:
Industry: Infrastructure
Quantitative Level: Easy
Qualitative Level: Medium

case_content.title: Prompt #1 - Revenue Growth Strategy
case_content.content: Cackalacky Construction is a small general contractor in the southeast US. They build schools exclusively. In 2016 Cackalacky generated $20M in revenue, but they have seen stagnant growth in recent years. Cackalacky Construction is looking to double their revenue in the next 3 years and has hired you to advise them how to do it.

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Prompt #1
case_content.content:
Provide only upon request:
- General contractors are responsible for all building activities but not design or engineering. They supervise subcontractors who perform physical construction work.
- Cackalacky clients are local governments that receive federal and state funding to build schools.
- Cackalacky only builds public schools and there are not any private clients.
- Cackalacky Construction has been in the southeast US for 20 years.
- Contractors who build schools in this region are facing similar problems.

Next step:
- The discussion on the initial framework should lead to analyzing potential markets to enter.
- Handover Exhibit #1 at that point.

case_content.title: Exhibit #1 - Potential Markets
case_content.content:
Exhibit #1: Potential Markets

| State | 2016 School Construction Funding ($M) | Population Growth | Major Industry | Literacy Rate | Projected YoY Funding Growth (^1) | Anticipated 3-Year Market Penetration (^2) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Michigan | 100 | 4% | Automotives | 87% | 10% | Med |
| Texas | 150 | 6% | Oil & Gas | 81% | 20% | Med |
| Georgia | 30 | 2% | Tourism | 73% | 50% | High |

Notes:
1. School construction funding.
2. Low = 5%; Med = 10%; High = 20%.

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Exhibit #1
case_content.content:
Exhibit #1 Guidance:

Analysis:
- The interviewee should do the math to get state funding, i.e. market size, for three years.
- Funding amount is the total market size for schools in the respective state; there is no other funding.
- Funding growth rate is the same every year for 3 years.
- Anticipated market penetration for Cackalacky is based on historical general contractor entrance into the market.
- Rounding is acceptable for funding dollars.
- It is important for the interviewee to remember the goal of doubling revenue in three years, meaning an additional $20M.

Potential time-consuming approach:
- The interviewee may multiply penetration rates for every year instead of just 2019.
- The interviewee should multiply 2019 state funding by the appropriate penetration rates.

Expected conclusions:
- Texas should offer the biggest market opportunity, $26M.
- Georgia should also meet the goal of doubling revenue by 2019, $20M.
- The interviewee should realize that Texas and Georgia meet the goal.
- The candidate should rationalize the best opportunity and provide a recommendation.

Projected funding and additional revenue:
| State | 2017 Funding | 2018 Funding | 2019 Funding | 2019 Cackalacky Projected Additional Revenue |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Michigan | $110M | $121M | $133M | $13M |
| Texas | $180M | $216M | $259M | $26M |
| Georgia | $45M | $68M | $101M | $20M |

case_content.title: Prompt #2 - Texas Market Entry
case_content.content:
Cackalacky Construction has decided to enter the Texas market.

What are some of the considerations to enter? What is the best way to enter the market?

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Prompt #2
case_content.content:
The interviewee needs a new framework, such as some form of Build, Borrow, Buy.

The considerations to enter should include understanding the market forces, including the competition.

When the discussion is around competition, handover Exhibit #2 and analyze the competitive landscape in Texas.

case_content.title: Exhibit #2 - Texas Competitive Landscape
case_content.content:
Exhibit #2: Texas Competitive Landscape

2015 Revenue from school construction ($M):
- General Contractor 1: $28M
- General Contractor 2: $21M
- General Contractor 3: $9M
- All Other: $92M

| Category | General Contractor 1 | General Contractor 2 | General Contractor 3 | All Other |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Market Share | 19% | 14% | 6% | 61% |
| School Specialty | Community College | K-12 | K-12 | All types |
| Years in Texas | 3 | 5 | 14 | 1-40 years |
| CAGR | 23% | 35% | 6% | 12% |

Notes:
1. General contractors with less than 5% of market.
2. Number of years general contractor has been building in Texas.

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Exhibit #2
case_content.content:
Exhibit #2 Guidance:

Analysis - Key Takeaways:
- The market is very fragmented.
- The top two players have entered the market in the past 5 years and are consolidating, based on relatively high CAGR.
- CAGR is extremely high.
- Candidate may look at acquisition targets or benchmark the strategy to General Contractor 1 / General Contractor 2 if applicable.
- Candidate may suggest finding a niche, relatively less crowded school market.

Additional guidance:
- Qualitative analysis is needed, not quantitative.
- The interviewer is looking for the interviewee to use his or her framework to analyze new information.
- The interviewee should give a recommendation on how to enter the market, based on analysis of the competitive landscape.

If asked:
- General Contractor 1 and General Contractor 2 both entered the market by acquiring several small players.

case_content.title: Prompt #3 - Challenges and Final Recommendation
case_content.content:
What are the potential challenges Cackalacky Construction will face as they enter the Texas market?

What are ways to mitigate some of these challenges?

What is the final recommendation?

case_content.title: Interviewer Guidance - Prompt #3
case_content.content:
Examples of potential challenges:
- Personnel.
- Legal and regulatory environment.
- Labor unions, although they do not exist in Texas.
- Industry relationships.
- IT integration.
- Language.
- Corporate culture.

The candidate should list different ways of entering the market with pros and cons of each, with a recommendation to evaluate each one of them.
